entries.speaker: belle-and-sebastian
entries.found: It was a combination of post-punk and embracing the beauty of the '60s and '70s: the Velvets , the Monkees , the Byrds , Love . That was in the blood.
entries.citation: Stuart Murdoch, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2015): "It was a combination of post-punk and embracing the beauty of the '60s and '70s: the Velvets, the Monkees, the Byrds, Love. That was in the blood."
entries.note: He says Belle and Sebastian's sound came from this mix; the Velvets are one of four named.

entries.speaker: belle-and-sebastian
entries.found: They were a real guide and made me think, "We need to get back to playing simple music again."
entries.citation: Stuart Murdoch, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2015): "They were a real guide and made me think, 'We need to get back to playing simple music again.'"

entries.speaker: blonde-redhead
entries.found: It was Lush and My Bloody Valentine. I went to those shows and I just remember falling apart every time. Like, “Oh my god, this is what I want to do. I want this noise.”
entries.citation: Kazu Makino, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2023): "It was Lush and My Bloody Valentine. I went to those shows and I just remember falling apart every time. Like, 'Oh my god, this is what I want to do. I want this noise.'"

entries.speaker: blonde-redhead
entries.found: It was Lush and My Bloody Valentine. I went to those shows and I just remember falling apart every time. Like, “Oh my god, this is what I want to do. I want this noise.”
entries.citation: Kazu Makino, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2023): "It was Lush and My Bloody Valentine. I went to those shows and I just remember falling apart every time. Like, 'Oh my god, this is what I want to do. I want this noise.'"

entries.speaker: blonde-redhead
entries.found: I never said it, but I felt like I was their student.
entries.citation: Kazu Makino, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2023): "I never said it, but I felt like I was their student."
entries.note: Also says "I really felt like the earth was shaking when I heard Unwound"; toured with them from 1995.

entries.speaker: blonde-redhead
entries.note: Says she loved Sonic Youth, Beck and Nirvana but "definitely didn't identify with" them.

entries.speaker: deerhunter
entries.found: I was totally amazed by that music.
entries.citation: Bradford Cox, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2009): "I was totally amazed by that music."
entries.note: Age 15, well before Deerhunter; he says it began his taste for hypnotic music.

entries.speaker: deerhunter
entries.note: Age 25, after Deerhunter was making records; says they summarize his upbringing but not that they shaped his work.

entries.speaker: caribou
entries.found: Kieran’s first Four Tet record had just come out at that point, and that was another revelation, because it was influenced by jazz, but not the shitty jazz that I would hear in a St. Germain record.
entries.citation: Dan Snaith, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2014): "Kieran’s first Four Tet record had just come out at that point, and that was another revelation, because it was influenced by jazz, but not the shitty jazz that I would hear in a St. Germain record."
entries.note: He also says Kieran Hebden "has become a huge part of what I've done musically"; sent his first demo to him.

entries.speaker: caribou
entries.note: Passing list of what he listened to before 20 ("stuff on the fringes... I was interested in music that deconstructed the rules"); strict reading is favourite, owner may upgrade.

entries.speaker: caribou
entries.note: Played their songs in his school band but says "I hated that music at the time".

entries.speaker: sleater-kinney
entries.found: The year before, Bikini Kill played one of their first shows in Olympia. My jaw hit the floor.
entries.citation: Corin Tucker, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2010): "The year before, Bikini Kill played one of their first shows in Olympia. My jaw hit the floor."
entries.note: Age 20 (1992), when she was in Heavens to Betsy, two years before Sleater-Kinney; she says their shows were visceral and she cried at them.

entries.speaker: galaxie-500
entries.found: We were listening to the Velvet Underground's self-titled third album-- almost to a crazy extreme.
entries.citation: Damon Krukowski and Naomi Yang, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2011): "We were listening to the Velvet Underground's self-titled third album-- almost to a crazy extreme."
entries.note: Both say it was so important while making On Fire (1989): "We were listening to records in a very different way than when we were just fans. As musicians, we wanted to inhabit that kind of sound."

entries.speaker: galaxie-500
entries.found: Big Star 's Third was very formative for all of us, too.
entries.citation: Damon Krukowski and Naomi Yang, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2011): "Big Star 's Third was very formative for all of us, too."

entries.speaker: galaxie-500
entries.found: Power, Corruption, & Lies was the college record for us. We listened to it endlessly.
entries.citation: Damon Krukowski and Naomi Yang, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2011): "Power, Corruption, & Lies was the college record for us. We listened to it endlessly."
entries.note: College years, before Galaxie 500 formed.

entries.speaker: galaxie-500
entries.note: Said of Damon & Naomi's own duo records, not Galaxie 500: "our next record was very much under the influence of Nick Drake and Tim Buckley and Fairport Convention."

entries.speaker: talking-heads
entries.found: The Velvet Underground were a big revelation.
entries.citation: David Byrne, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2018): "The Velvet Underground were a big revelation."
entries.note: Learned and covered their songs in his Providence band before Talking Heads.

entries.speaker: destroyer
entries.found: When Slanted and Enchanted came out, everything changed.
entries.citation: Dan Bejar, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2012): "When Slanted and Enchanted came out, everything changed."
entries.note: Also: "That's when I bought an electric guitar and an amplifier. I was 21."

entries.speaker: destroyer
entries.found: At 15, I was deep in the clutches of the Jesus and Mary Chain.
entries.citation: Dan Bejar, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2012): "At 15, I was deep in the clutches of the Jesus and Mary Chain."
entries.note: "That was the first noisy thing I liked"; formative taste, not tied explicitly to his own music.

entries.speaker: destroyer
entries.note: Says he wasn't that into In Utero; it is remembered as a 10th-birthday gift.

entries.speaker: destroyer
entries.note: "I pretended to like American college rock like R.E.M. or the Replacements or Hüsker Dü or whatever, but I didn't get it."

entries.speaker: vampire-weekend
entries.found: I was already really into the first album.
entries.citation: Ezra Koenig, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2010): "I was already really into the first album."
entries.note: Fan and briefly intern at the Walkmen's studio before Vampire Weekend: "I was really obsessed."

entries.speaker: portishead
entries.found: And that record just triggered a whole new part of my life.
entries.citation: Geoff Barrow, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2009): "And that record just triggered a whole new part of my life."
entries.note: Ege Bamyasi; says it "led into the next record [Third], the start of the shaping of it."

entries.speaker: portishead
entries.found: I think Silver Apples have been more inspirational, but then I'd say that it's a two-horse race on that one.
entries.citation: Geoff Barrow, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2009): "I think Silver Apples have been more inspirational, but then I'd say that it's a two-horse race on that one."
entries.note: Said at 35 (c.2007), about the impact on him as Portishead worked on Third.

entries.speaker: black-flag
entries.found: But through the Stooges, I got in my mind that it’s Black Flag versus the audience.
entries.citation: Henry Rollins, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2019): "But through the Stooges, I got in my mind that it’s Black Flag versus the audience."
entries.note: Also: "the Stooges kind of gave me my posture." Fun House heard in the van after joining Black Flag in 1981.

entries.speaker: black-flag
entries.found: Alan Vega was a hero to me growing up because of the first Suicide record.
entries.citation: Henry Rollins, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2019): "Alan Vega was a hero to me growing up because of the first Suicide record."
entries.note: Hero "growing up" (before Black Flag); Rollins Band later covered "Ghost Rider".

entries.speaker: black-flag
entries.note: Cop EP "blew my mind" in 1984, but he doesn't say it changed Black Flag's music.

entries.speaker: interpol
entries.found: Nirvana helped me understand that music was what I wanted to do with my life.
entries.citation: Paul Banks, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2018): "Nirvana helped me understand that music was what I wanted to do with my life."

entries.speaker: interpol
entries.note: Only: a teacher "helped me and my friends get into Bob Dylan".

entries.speaker: spiritualized
entries.found: I got lucky, because my whole life premise and what I do is kind of built around that record.
entries.citation: Jason Pierce (J Spaceman), in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2012): "I got lucky, because my whole life premise and what I do is kind of built around that record."
entries.note: Raw Power.

entries.speaker: spiritualized
entries.note: Only: "It wasn't all about the Stooges or the Velvet Underground for me anymore."

entries.speaker: pulp
entries.found: If you listen to that first Pulp record, it is just a direct rip off of his first album—though I’m not saying it was as good as that.
entries.citation: Jarvis Cocker, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2017): "If you listen to that first Pulp record, it is just a direct rip off of his first album—though I’m not saying it was as good as that."
entries.note: Also: Cohen and Scott Walker are "the two real touchstones in terms of people I’ve listened to consistently throughout my whole life."

entries.speaker: pulp
entries.note: Only: a Velvet Underground record was on when his son was in the room.

entries.speaker: sex-pistols
entries.found: And I had little time for what was coming out of America; bands like Television never really grabbed me, I just couldn’t connect.
entries.citation: John Lydon, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2016): "And I had little time for what was coming out of America; bands like Television never really grabbed me, I just couldn’t connect."
entries.note: Says they "never really grabbed me"; not a denial of influence in so many words, but he rules them out.

entries.speaker: the-smiths
entries.found: When we did The Queen Is Dead , I was trying to evoke Raw Power 's overall feeling of beautiful solitude: It was OK to be broke and not have much but your records.
entries.citation: Johnny Marr, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2012): "When we did The Queen Is Dead, I was trying to evoke Raw Power 's overall feeling of beautiful solitude: It was OK to be broke and not have much but your records."

entries.speaker: the-smiths
entries.note: Low was a "touchstone" for Marr and Bernard Sumner when they formed Electronic in 1988, not the Smiths.

entries.speaker: the-smiths
entries.note: "I want to form a group that sounds like this" came in the late 90s, after the Smiths.

entries.speaker: yeah-yeah-yeahs
entries.note: Only: "I’ve always dug the Velvet Underground... but it wasn’t until my thirties that I fell in love with Lou Reed."

entries.speaker: bikini-kill
entries.found: The quality of sound was really influential for me.
entries.citation: Kathleen Hanna, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2013): "The quality of sound was really influential for me."
entries.note: Said of The Real Janelle EP, which she says was produced much better than Bikini Kill's records.

entries.speaker: kurt-vile
entries.found: Around '93, the radio started playing "Loser" by Beck and "Cut Your Hair" by Pavement, and then I got way into Pavement.
entries.citation: Kurt Vile, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2009): "Around '93, the radio started playing 'Loser' by Beck and 'Cut Your Hair' by Pavement, and then I got way into Pavement."
entries.note: "That was kind of a gateway drug into indie rock." Aged about 13, years before his own recordings.

entries.speaker: kurt-vile
entries.note: Listened "so much" in the mid-2000s while already making his own music.

entries.speaker: sonic-youth
entries.found: At the time, that was very important to my re-involvement with music, which had gotten so bombastic, serving larger audiences and scenes and big stadium concerts.
entries.citation: Lee Ranaldo, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2012): "At the time, that was very important to my re-involvement with music, which had gotten so bombastic, serving larger audiences and scenes and big stadium concerts."
entries.note: Marquee Moon; he and the friends he later played music with "got ahold of Marquee Moon" in college and "it knocked us all out."

entries.speaker: sonic-youth
entries.found: There was a time when I could play almost every song on that record on my guitar.
entries.citation: Lee Ranaldo, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2012): "There was a time when I could play almost every song on that record on my guitar."
entries.note: After the Gold Rush; "In many ways, he set the tone for acoustic guitar players."

entries.speaker: sonic-youth
entries.found: For kids of my generation, they (along with Dylan) were the life-changing event.
entries.citation: Lee Ranaldo, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2012): "For kids of my generation, they (along with Dylan) were the life-changing event."
entries.note: Childhood; "To me, Dylan's music is the paramount musical expression of a single individual."

entries.speaker: sonic-youth
entries.found: We were very energized by it.
entries.citation: Lee Ranaldo, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2012): "We were very energized by it."
entries.note: Said of the early-80s SST/American hardcore movement; "the Minutemen always represented something a little bit closer to my heart." Sonic Youth had formed in 1981.

entries.speaker: liz-phair
entries.found: Guyville wouldn’t be Guyville without the Human League.
entries.citation: Liz Phair, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2023): "Guyville wouldn’t be Guyville without the Human League."
entries.note: "It also became really formative for me, because it was the first time I had heard a woman clapping back in a song."

entries.speaker: liz-phair
entries.found: It was my gateway drug into alternative.
entries.citation: Liz Phair, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2023): "It was my gateway drug into alternative."
entries.note: Sister, c.1987; "Sonic Youth was the first time that I saw ugly sounds made gorgeous."

entries.speaker: liz-phair
entries.found: Slanted and Enchanted felt like someone doing what I had inside my heart to do, and it was my war call.
entries.citation: Liz Phair, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2023): "Slanted and Enchanted felt like someone doing what I had inside my heart to do, and it was my war call."
entries.note: Was on repeat on her Walkman while she made Exile in Guyville.

entries.speaker: lucinda-williams
entries.found: Especially Neil Young ’s Everybody Knows This Is Nowhere ; he’s a huge influence.
entries.citation: Lucinda Williams, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2020): "Especially Neil Young ’s Everybody Knows This Is Nowhere; he’s a huge influence."

entries.speaker: lucinda-williams
entries.note: Fell "madly in love" with them c.1977-78 and "the first band that I'd heard that I could relate to"; no claim they shaped her own songs.

entries.speaker: superchunk
entries.note: Power, Corruption and Lies at 14: "It was the weirdest record I had ever bought... Now it’s one of my top five records of all time." No claim it shaped Superchunk.

entries.speaker: mary-timony
entries.found: That totally changed my life, and after that, I went to every punk show that was going on and hung out with punk kids.
entries.citation: Mary Timony, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2014): "That totally changed my life, and after that, I went to every punk show that was going on and hung out with punk kids."
entries.note: Her first punk show, Rites of Spring and Beefeater, Jan 1985; "my favorite band from that time was Rites of Spring, and it still is."

entries.speaker: mary-timony
entries.found: That record changed the way I thought of music completely.
entries.citation: Mary Timony, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2014): "That record changed the way I thought of music completely."

entries.speaker: rem
entries.found: I had this epiphany and realized that this is what I wanted to do with my life: learn how to sing and start a band.
entries.citation: Michael Stipe, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2021): "I had this epiphany and realized that this is what I wanted to do with my life: learn how to sing and start a band."
entries.note: Horses, bought the day it came out, aged 15.

entries.speaker: rem
entries.found: There were all these records that came out around then that were so profoundly important.
entries.citation: Michael Stipe, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2021): "There were all these records that came out around then that were so profoundly important."
entries.note: Said as R.E.M. were forming (1980); the B-52's told them "You gotta hear this unbelievable record by this band called Joy Division."

entries.speaker: rem
entries.found: There were all these records that came out around then that were so profoundly important.
entries.citation: Michael Stipe, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2021): "There were all these records that came out around then that were so profoundly important."
entries.note: Names Wire's 154 in the same passage ("That was very shocking"); the sentence covers the group of records, not Wire alone.

entries.speaker: rem
entries.note: Named with the New York Dolls, Ramones, Blondie and Talking Heads as the CBGB scene he identified with at 15 ("a place where I felt a kinship"); not tied to his own music beyond the scene.

entries.speaker: mogwai
entries.found: The Cure, the Jesus and Mary Chain, and the Cult were the first bands I became really obsessed with.
entries.citation: Stuart Braithwaite, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2011): "The Cure, the Jesus and Mary Chain, and the Cult were the first bands I became really obsessed with."

entries.speaker: mogwai
entries.found: The Cure, the Jesus and Mary Chain, and the Cult were the first bands I became really obsessed with.
entries.citation: Stuart Braithwaite, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2011): "The Cure, the Jesus and Mary Chain, and the Cult were the first bands I became really obsessed with."

entries.speaker: mogwai
entries.found: But when I look through the records that came out in 1996, the one that had a massive effect was Richard D. James Album by Aphex Twin.
entries.citation: Stuart Braithwaite, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2011): "But when I look through the records that came out in 1996, the one that had a massive effect was Richard D. James Album by Aphex Twin."
entries.note: "This was just when Mogwai started."

entries.speaker: mogwai
entries.found: We were interested in a lot of American rock bands like Sonic Youth and Slint, as well as 70s guitar bands like the Stooges and Television.
entries.citation: Stuart Braithwaite, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2011): "We were interested in a lot of American rock bands like Sonic Youth and Slint, as well as 70s guitar bands like the Stooges and Television."
entries.note: "This was just when Mogwai started." "Interested in" is a mild claim.

entries.speaker: mogwai
entries.found: We were interested in a lot of American rock bands like Sonic Youth and Slint, as well as 70s guitar bands like the Stooges and Television.
entries.citation: Stuart Braithwaite, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2011): "We were interested in a lot of American rock bands like Sonic Youth and Slint, as well as 70s guitar bands like the Stooges and Television."
entries.note: As for Sonic Youth.

entries.speaker: mogwai
entries.found: We were interested in a lot of American rock bands like Sonic Youth and Slint, as well as 70s guitar bands like the Stooges and Television.
entries.citation: Stuart Braithwaite, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2011): "We were interested in a lot of American rock bands like Sonic Youth and Slint, as well as 70s guitar bands like the Stooges and Television."
entries.note: As for Sonic Youth.

entries.speaker: mogwai
entries.found: We were interested in a lot of American rock bands like Sonic Youth and Slint, as well as 70s guitar bands like the Stooges and Television.
entries.citation: Stuart Braithwaite, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2011): "We were interested in a lot of American rock bands like Sonic Youth and Slint, as well as 70s guitar bands like the Stooges and Television."
entries.note: As for Sonic Youth.

entries.speaker: mogwai
entries.note: Seen at Reading 1991 aged 15; "inspiring to see that music infiltrating the mainstream" but not about his own music.

entries.speaker: mogwai
entries.note: Unimpressed: "a carbon copy of a ton of old bands".

entries.speaker: of-montreal
entries.found: I saw what was possible, like, if these guys can do it, I can too.
entries.citation: Kevin Barnes, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2010): "I saw what was possible, like, if these guys can do it, I can too."
entries.note: About the Elephant 6 bands in Athens; "That's where I learned that DIY approach to music making."

entries.speaker: of-montreal
entries.found: I saw what was possible, like, if these guys can do it, I can too.
entries.citation: Kevin Barnes, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2010): "I saw what was possible, like, if these guys can do it, I can too."
entries.note: As for Neutral Milk Hotel.

entries.speaker: of-montreal
entries.note: Named in a list of records he discovered at 15; only Stevie Wonder is singled out as inspiring.

entries.speaker: descendents
entries.found: Bad Brains had put out the “Pay to Cum” single in 1980, and that had a huge effect on us.
entries.citation: Milo Aukerman, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2016): "Bad Brains had put out the 'Pay to Cum' single in 1980, and that had a huge effect on us."
entries.note: "We wanted to play as fast as humanly possible but still be tight."

entries.speaker: descendents
entries.found: I started out with X, and then I graduated to the Germs, and then Black Flag.
entries.citation: Milo Aukerman, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2016): "I started out with X, and then I graduated to the Germs, and then Black Flag."
entries.note: "So I went from being obsessed with L.A. punk rock to being a part of it." Strict reading: scene-level obsession just before joining the Descendents.

entries.speaker: ride
entries.found: That was the gig where I was like, "Right, this is what I'm going to do with my life."
entries.citation: Andy Bell, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2011): "That was the gig where I was like, 'Right, this is what I'm going to do with my life.'"
entries.note: Also: "I was a keen guitar player, so Johnny Marr was my first teacher, really."

entries.speaker: ride
entries.found: Looking back, I would say that if you go somewhere down the middle between those two albums, you get what Ride was all about.
entries.citation: Andy Bell, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2011): "Looking back, I would say that if you go somewhere down the middle between those two albums, you get what Ride was all about."
entries.note: Between Isn't Anything and the Stone Roses' debut.

entries.speaker: ride
entries.found: Stone Roses was another seismic shift in my musical taste.
entries.citation: Andy Bell, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2011): "Stone Roses was another seismic shift in my musical taste."
entries.note: Also: "if you go somewhere down the middle between those two albums, you get what Ride was all about."

entries.speaker: ride
entries.note: Says they remind him of early Ride; he is a new fan.

entries.speaker: spoon
entries.found: I had really come around to Wire and Talking Heads around this time too, and I started to like that kind of abstract lyrical imagery more than literal story telling.
entries.citation: Britt Daniel, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2018): "I had really come around to Wire and Talking Heads around this time too, and I started to like that kind of abstract lyrical imagery more than literal story telling."
entries.note: "It made it easier to write lyrics". Around the time of Telephono (1996).

entries.speaker: spoon
entries.found: I had really come around to Wire and Talking Heads around this time too, and I started to like that kind of abstract lyrical imagery more than literal story telling.
entries.citation: Britt Daniel, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2018): "I had really come around to Wire and Talking Heads around this time too, and I started to like that kind of abstract lyrical imagery more than literal story telling."
entries.note: As for Wire.

entries.speaker: spoon
entries.note: "I didn't know a lot about what Stephen Malkmus was singing about, but it fucking worked."

entries.speaker: bright-eyes
entries.found: For better or worse, it totally changed my life.
entries.citation: Conor Oberst, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2020): "For better or worse, it totally changed my life."
entries.note: Also: "I think everybody is a combination of their influences, but Townes is the deep, dark part that I carry around."

entries.speaker: bright-eyes
entries.found: I got really into Elliott Smith around that same period.
entries.citation: Conor Oberst, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2020): "I got really into Elliott Smith around that same period."
entries.note: Mid-teens, when he was writing folk-type songs; "When you’re young, it’s easy to romanticize the tortured artist kinda thing. I absolutely fell for it."

entries.speaker: bright-eyes
entries.found: The Replacements were his favorite band of all time, but that song in particular was special.
entries.citation: Conor Oberst, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2020): "The Replacements were his favorite band of all time, but that song in particular was special."
entries.note: His brother's favourite; the brother taught him "Here Comes a Regular" when he was learning guitar at 10. The wording is about the brother's love; weak.

entries.speaker: cat-power
entries.note: Bootleg Series track in a lover's bedroom: "validated my pain"; nothing about her own music.

entries.speaker: wilco
entries.found: They felt attainable.
entries.citation: Jeff Tweedy, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2018): "They felt attainable."
entries.note: Also: they "were making music with so few moving parts that you could hear what was going on and learn what each instrument was doing" and "That was liberating for kids like me" -- said of the time he started writing songs and playing shows.

entries.speaker: wilco
entries.note: "The big three for me are Bob Dylan, Neil Young, and Johnny Cash." Strong, but no time frame or link to his work.

entries.speaker: wilco
entries.note: As for Neil Young.

entries.speaker: the-walkmen
entries.note: His earlier band the Recoys covered "I'm Straight"; "It just really hit home with me" but he also calls imitating it "such a bad idea".

entries.speaker: vashti-bunyan
entries.found: It also made me want to be a wandering singer myself.
entries.citation: Vashti Bunyan, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2014): "It also made me want to be a wandering singer myself."
entries.note: The Freewheelin' Bob Dylan; "it opened my mind and educated me more than anything else had ever done."

entries.speaker: vashti-bunyan
entries.note: She says Joni "seemed to say everything that I’d ever wanted to say or do" but it made her stop making music for 30 years.

entries.speaker: wire
entries.found: We studiously ignored Joy Division because they seemed a little too derivative of us.
entries.citation: Colin Newman, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2017): "We studiously ignored Joy Division because they seemed a little too derivative of us."
entries.note: Said of 1979.

entries.speaker: wire
entries.found: We didn’t have anything to do with Gang of Four.
entries.citation: Colin Newman, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2017): "We didn’t have anything to do with Gang of Four."
entries.note: "They were coming from a very different place."

entries.speaker: yo-la-tengo
entries.found: At that point, Damaged by Black Flag had great sway over me and to this day it still does.
entries.citation: Yo La Tengo (James McNew, Ira Kaplan, Georgia Hubley), in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2018): "At that point, Damaged by Black Flag had great sway over me and to this day it still does."
entries.note: James McNew at 15, before joining Yo La Tengo in 1991; "Black Flag were a natural extension of my childhood love of hard rock."

entries.speaker: yo-la-tengo
entries.found: My ninth grade English teacher was married to someone who wrote for Creem , and she lent me [the Velvet Underground’s] White Light/White Heat and [Lenny Kaye’s garage rock compilation] Nuggets . After I discovered that direction, I tanked every class.
entries.citation: Yo La Tengo (James McNew, Ira Kaplan, Georgia Hubley), in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2018): "My ninth grade English teacher was married to someone who wrote for Creem, and she lent me [the Velvet Underground’s] White Light/White Heat and [Lenny Kaye’s garage rock compilation] Nuggets. After I discovered that direction, I tanked every class."
entries.note: James McNew, formative years. Also Ira Kaplan says their love of the Clean was so great Hubley guessed they'd miss the Velvet Underground.

offMap.name: Felt
offMap.sentence: I had an obsession with Felt , an indie band that stayed with me all the way through the '90s.

offMap.name: The Byrds
offMap.sentence: It was a combination of post-punk and embracing the beauty of the '60s and '70s: the Velvets , the Monkees , the Byrds , Love . That was in the blood.

offMap.name: The Monkees
offMap.sentence: It was a combination of post-punk and embracing the beauty of the '60s and '70s: the Velvets , the Monkees , the Byrds , Love . That was in the blood.

offMap.name: Love
offMap.sentence: It was a combination of post-punk and embracing the beauty of the '60s and '70s: the Velvets , the Monkees , the Byrds , Love . That was in the blood.

offMap.name: The Rolling Stones
offMap.sentence: I started to sneak home music from classmates during junior high, and I became obsessed.

offMap.name: Les Rita Mitsouko
offMap.sentence: You just get hit by this music like lightning without knowing any backstory or cultural reference points, and you’re instantly converted.

offMap.name: Serge Gainsbourg
offMap.sentence: For many years, that was my Bible.

offMap.name: Terry Riley
offMap.sentence: Those two had huge impacts on me, but Terry was someone I would always listen to during that period and wonder how something could be so moving.

offMap.name: Ryuichi Sakamoto
offMap.sentence: Those two had huge impacts on me, but Terry was someone I would always listen to during that period and wonder how something could be so moving.

offMap.name: Danny Elfman
offMap.sentence: I became really interested in the way melodies can be so heartbreaking or nostalgic or melancholy.

offMap.name: Steve Reich
offMap.sentence: This was the period when I was obsessed with noise and 20th century composers, just obscure shit, half of which I don't really remember.

offMap.name: The Orb
offMap.sentence: Pretty shortly after I was introduced to that Orb CD, I got a little sampler and a keyboard, and was making electronic music myself.

offMap.name: Albert Ayler
offMap.sentence: Albert Ayler's Spiritual Unity is still one of my favorite records.

offMap.name: Sun Ra
offMap.sentence: I was less interested in the conventional jazz music that I’d been taught by my teachers in high school and more interested in this amazing stuff I had no idea existed before, like Pharoah Sanders , Sun Ra , Alice Coltrane , and late John Coltrane .

offMap.name: Theo Parrish
offMap.sentence: It was a catalytic moment for me that reinvigorated my interest in dance music.

offMap.name: The B-52's
offMap.sentence: I think the B-52's were a huge influence on Sleater-Kinney.

offMap.name: Joan Jett
offMap.sentence: I thought Joan Jett was amazing.

offMap.name: The Dream Syndicate
offMap.sentence: Another hugely important record was The Days of Wine and Roses by the Dream Syndicate.

offMap.name: Elvis Costello
offMap.sentence: I was obsessed with Elvis Costello's Armed Forces .

offMap.name: Robert Wyatt
offMap.sentence: Robert Wyatt's such a great model for that.
offMap.note: Said of Damon & Naomi's duo records after Galaxie 500.

offMap.name: Fairport Convention
offMap.sentence: our next record was very much under the influence of Nick Drake and Tim Buckley and Fairport Convention.
offMap.note: Damon & Naomi duo record after Galaxie 500.

offMap.name: The Byrds
offMap.sentence: Hearing that, I realized: I have to get out of here, because there are people in other places.

offMap.name: Woody Guthrie
offMap.sentence: That was something to realize at a young age: that a song could do that.

offMap.name: Parliament
offMap.sentence: In Talking Heads, the record collection was filled with Hamilton Bohannon, James Brown, Roxy Music, Funkadelic, and P-Funk, that whole world.

offMap.name: Scott Walker
offMap.sentence: The bulk of 2003 was very much me wrestling with my intense love of Scott Walker.

offMap.name: Plush
offMap.sentence: At the time, I was really inspired by More You Becomes You by the group Plush.

offMap.name: Roxy Music
offMap.sentence: I got lost in Avalon in an unhealthy way: the reverbs, the drum sounds, the percussion.

offMap.name: A Tribe Called Quest
offMap.sentence: When I was 15, this was one of the albums that I listened to constantly.

offMap.name: Gang Starr
offMap.sentence: DJ Premier is my hero, my DJ hero.

offMap.name: Wu-Tang Clan
offMap.sentence: He hugely inspired me.
offMap.note: Said of RZA; also "I was trying to rip him off."

offMap.name: Sunn O)))
offMap.sentence: Both those bands, I would say, were part of the impact back then.

offMap.name: Madlib
offMap.sentence: The Jaylib record is absolutely massive in my head.

offMap.name: John Coltrane
offMap.sentence: So Coltrane made me aspire to just be musically pure, and it’s the jazz guys that informed my musical integrity: If you don’t like it, don’t play it.

offMap.name: John Frusciante
offMap.sentence: That’s John Frusciante’s influence.
offMap.note: He says his delay technique on Interpol's "Leif Erikson" comes from Frusciante's Niandra LaDes.

offMap.name: Aerosmith
offMap.sentence: I had to learn how to play it so I could get even closer to that music.
offMap.note: Said of "Dream On"; led him to pick up guitar.

offMap.name: The Cramps
offMap.sentence: But at this stage we were listening to the Cramps , the Gun Club-- this very primitive sound.
offMap.note: Said of the years he started playing in bands.

offMap.name: The Gun Club
offMap.sentence: But at this stage we were listening to the Cramps , the Gun Club-- this very primitive sound.

offMap.name: The Staple Singers
offMap.sentence: All that lyrical content that I've always thought came from the Staple Singers is all in groups like Dion & the Belmonts , the Dixie Nightingales , the Chantels -- the whole thing is built around that.

offMap.name: Sun Ra
offMap.sentence: The MC5 always talked about Sun Ra , who introduced me to a whole world into free-form music.

offMap.name: Devo
offMap.sentence: The first Devo album came out that year [in 1978], and I went to see them play at the City Hall in Sheffield, which was quite influential.
offMap.note: He adds that Pulp learned the Devo song "Gut Feeling" early on.

offMap.name: Scott Walker
offMap.sentence: Leonard Cohen and Scott Walker are the two real touchstones in terms of people I’ve listened to consistently throughout my whole life.

offMap.name: Miles Davis
offMap.sentence: So that's what I got from Miles. I finally got improvisation.

offMap.name: La Monte Young
offMap.sentence: We learned about discipline and working every day from La Monte, about not particularly forcing anything to happen, but allowing things to happen.
offMap.note: Played with him in the Dream Syndicate.

offMap.name: John Cage
offMap.sentence: That's when I found La Monte Young, and Cage, and "4'33"" , which threw another spanner in the works, because it was really about how environment impacts performance.

offMap.name: Captain Beefheart
offMap.sentence: That was my confirmation. From then on, there was room for everything.
offMap.note: Trout Mask Replica, around age 10-15.

offMap.name: The Rolling Stones
offMap.sentence: the Stones became one of the blueprints for what I wanted to do with a group.
offMap.note: "I took a lot of that into the Smiths."

offMap.name: T. Rex
offMap.sentence: That feeling was something I wanted to create in music.
offMap.note: Said of "Metal Guru" seen on Top of the Pops, aged 10.

offMap.name: Liars
offMap.sentence: It taught me a valuable career lesson, that change is important and good, and you don’t need to feel the pressure to make the same record twice.
offMap.note: Said of They Were Wrong So We Drowned.

offMap.name: Michael Jackson
offMap.sentence: His sparkly gloves left a deep impression on me—when we started the Yeah Yeah Yeahs, I would always wear a glove on my right hand as my nod to Michael.

offMap.name: Jefferson Airplane
offMap.sentence: I listened to that and accessed my inner freak.

offMap.name: Public Enemy
offMap.sentence: I wanted to put myself out there because they did.
offMap.note: Listened to It Takes a Nation of Millions on tour as Bikini Kill started.

offMap.name: Free Kitten
offMap.sentence: I was wondering, "What do I want my next band to sound like?" And those questions made me think about being able to write whatever I wanted
offMap.note: Her next-band thinking at 35 (Le Tigre era), after Bikini Kill.

offMap.name: The Grateful Dead
offMap.sentence: I always valued both of those aspects in what Sonic Youth has done through the years-- being able to get very abstract and very concrete within the same song.
offMap.note: Said of Europe '72, which he calls "super influential".

offMap.name: The Beatles
offMap.sentence: Their music still inspires me in a million different ways, from the complexity of their later work in the studio to the sheer amazing songwriting.

offMap.name: The Kinks
offMap.sentence: I go through the window and enter that dimension and I’m there, full of suspension of disbelief, trying to figure it out.
offMap.note: Said after "Tired of Waiting for You"; "that was the beginning of my music career."

offMap.name: Missy Elliott
offMap.sentence: She was the light in the front of my boat as I was going through a scary, dark swamp, career-wise.
offMap.note: "I started taking producing seriously after that."

offMap.name: The Pretenders
offMap.sentence: The Pretenders were a huge influence on me because they were straight-ahead rock music with great lyrics.

offMap.name: Rev. Pearly Brown
offMap.sentence: This was the first blues album that really influenced me.

offMap.name: Buffalo Springfield
offMap.sentence: Stephen Stills and Neil Young were in the band, and their solo music has really inspired me, too.

offMap.name: Polvo
offMap.sentence: I learned a lot from Ash and tried to emulate his style in my own music.
offMap.note: Said of Ash Bowie, guitarist of Helium and Polvo.

offMap.name: The Slits
offMap.sentence: I'd listen to the Slits’ Cut on a cassette a lot in that car.

offMap.name: The B-52's
offMap.sentence: That first B-52’s album still hasn’t gotten the recognition that it deserves as one of the most groundbreaking and influential records of all time—most certainly on me and everyone around the Athens scene.

offMap.name: Pylon
offMap.sentence: I definitely pulled a great deal from them.
offMap.note: Said of Athens band Pylon's art-school approach.

offMap.name: Bardo Pond
offMap.sentence: They seemed to be doing something really amazing with rock music-- free, brutal, but also calm.

offMap.name: The Cult
offMap.sentence: The Cure, the Jesus and Mary Chain, and the Cult were the first bands I became really obsessed with.

offMap.name: Os Mutantes
offMap.sentence: the first three Os Mutantes records taught me the potential of a song arrangement and that it doesn't have to be linear in any way.

offMap.name: Stevie Wonder
offMap.sentence: Stevie was a beacon, like, "OK, this is what you can do if you keep working at it."

offMap.name: X
offMap.sentence: X really does symbolize a shift for me into L.A. punk rock and immersing myself in that scene.

offMap.name: The Germs
offMap.sentence: I started out with X, and then I graduated to the Germs, and then Black Flag.

offMap.name: Tom Lehrer
offMap.sentence: to be able to poke fun at others, and at yourself, is an important part of what the Descendents do as a band.

offMap.name: The Beatles
offMap.sentence: It’s hard to deny the DNA that came from the Beatles when you look at what the Descendents did as a band later—that whole sense of melody, that whole sense of pop music.

offMap.name: Bow Wow Wow
offMap.sentence: then I really got into Bow Wow Wow , who were a huge influence.
offMap.note: "hearing women in music that would eventually lead me to thinking I might be able to do this myself."

offMap.name: Babes in Toyland
offMap.sentence: Babes in Toyland came before riot grrrl and had a huge influence on a lot of us: These strong, kickass women playing fierce music.

offMap.name: The Slits
offMap.sentence: The Slits have been hugely influential on me—this awesome band of women who created something out of nothing.

offMap.name: Mecca Normal
offMap.sentence: “Strong White Male” was an anthem of mine.

offMap.name: Prince
offMap.sentence: That song became what a single was to me—something stripped down, so you could focus on a few key elements that were just perfect.
offMap.note: Said of "Kiss".

offMap.name: PJ Harvey
offMap.sentence: I still reference To Bring You My Love when we make records.

offMap.name: The Kinks
offMap.sentence: A song like “The Fitted Shirt” would not have existed without the Kinks.

offMap.name: Cliff Martinez
offMap.sentence: You could draw a line from this soundtrack to “The Ghost of You Lingers” from Ga Ga Ga Ga Ga , which came out around this time.
offMap.note: Solaris soundtrack.

offMap.name: Wu-Tang Clan
offMap.sentence: In high school we would listen to Wu-Tang Clan, and I always thought the skits and in-between things were cool—that was something we stole from hip-hop and tried to put into our records.

offMap.name: Flat Duo Jets
offMap.sentence: when I saw and heard Flat Duo Jets with Dexter Romweber, all my dreams came true.
offMap.note: Aged 16; "When you’re at a show like that, you don’t think anything, you’re just learning."

offMap.name: Aretha Franklin
offMap.sentence: I was forever changed by that performance.
offMap.note: Aged about 12.

offMap.name: King Crimson
offMap.sentence: In the period before I was living in London, I saw King Crimson more than any other band, and they had the biggest effect on me.

offMap.name: Todd Rundgren
offMap.sentence: I had never heard anything like A Wizard in my life.
offMap.note: "It was bonkers but it totally primed me for what was next."

offMap.name: The Clean
offMap.sentence: the Clean’s Compilation cassette completely blew our minds when we got it in the late ’80s.
offMap.note: Said by Ira Kaplan.
